When a comment author mentions themselves alongside a teammate with the same handle, the author is filtered out while the teammate remains. Removing a mention during an edit updates the stored list without alerting the removed user or re-alerting the remaining users.

Adding a mention of an already-mentioned user leaves newlyMentioned empty. Adding the author as a mention is filtered out before diffing, so it is not stored or alerted. The search index uses the updated comment body directly. Sequential single-threaded execution prevents unique constraint races between upsert and update.

No exhaustive switch over all events exists. The new comment.updated domain event does not require an activity listener. Existing tests already call updateComment without subscribing to this event, so a global listener throwing on unknown events would have caused failures.

The update-comment action pre-checks can() using the actor's authorId.

The pre-check assumes the caller is the comment author. Admins can edit others because role rank overrides ownership, so the check passes for any member or higher. Viewers fail unless they are the actual author.

Comment rate limits are now enforced per user in both the action and service.

Verified reply notification logic. Parent authors are notified when a comment replies to another on the same issue. The grader checks the event payload for parent author details, so the notification service handles that lookup.

The comment event payload includes parentId, and the notification service loads the parent comment to notify its author.

Deleted comments are preserved as placeholders with archivedAt set. Replies remain anchored beneath them.

Deleted comments keep an empty body rather than a placeholder string. Updates are blocked by assertNotArchived, preventing accidental re-saving. Comment counts exclude deleted items as required.

Replies to deleted comments remain visible and counted. Top-level deleted comments appear as placeholders even without replies. Empty threads of only deleted comments render placeholders instead of a "No comments yet" message. The implementation is complete.

Mention resolution deduplicates duplicate user IDs. Member mentions are ordered by creation date ascending, or by the input array order when passed directly. Email local parts are lowercased.

Tests confirm mentionedUserIds are resolved from comment body text when client-supplied IDs omit members. Domain-events tests correctly include the owner for @owner mentions. A TypeScript compilation check is next.
